months.title: march
months.subtitle: the waiting begins
months.narrative: The snow is still melting and the balcony is bare, but inside, something is stirring. Seeds are soaking, the trays are filling up, and the heat mat is humming. This is the month of patience and tiny beginnings.

tasks.text: refrigerate pansy seeds for 7 days
start cold-stratifying delphinium seeds
start cold-stratifying lavender seeds
surface sow all 30 rosemary seeds — patience with this one
sow tomato sweetie on heat mat (march 20)
sow calendula, aster, alyssum, marigold (march 20)
sow snapdragon in 16-tray — no heat pad, surface sow (march 20)
set up the heat mat and grow light
check that all seed packets are accounted for
order peat pellets if running low

months.title: april
months.subtitle: something is happening
months.narrative: The trays are filling up with green. Sprouts are pushing through and the apartment smells like damp earth. April is the month where the garden stops being theoretical and becomes real.

tasks.text: sow basil (sweet, thai, tulsi) on heat mat (april 3)
sow oregano, thyme, chives (april 3)
soak parsley seeds 24h, then sow (april 3)
sow chamomile — surface sow, mist gently
sow valerian — surface sow, press lightly
sow yarrow — surface sow, barely press
cold-stratify echinacea 7 days, then sow in 16-tray (dark)
cold-stratify shiso 7–10 days, then sow
sow swiss chard, kale, mint (april 3)
sow lettuce and spinach in 16-tray (april 3)
soak and scarify lupine seeds — careful, they're toxic
sow arugula (april 17)
check all march sowings for sprouts
thin crowded seedlings if needed
start shopping for soil ingredients and pots

months.title: may
months.subtitle: the balcony opens
months.narrative: May 15 is the day. The last frost passes and everything moves outside. The hardening-off dance begins a week early — trays go out for a few hours, then come back in. By month's end, the balcony is alive.

tasks.text: begin hardening off seedlings (may 8 — one week before transplant)
mix all soil recipes (A through G)
set up all containers on the balcony
transplant everything on may 15
direct sow cilantro and dill in C9B
soak nasturtium seeds 12–24h, then direct sow in C9
water everything deeply after transplanting
install tomato cage or stakes in C1
check railing brackets are secure
take a photo of the fresh balcony

months.title: june
months.subtitle: the garden fills in
months.narrative: The containers are settling in. Roots are reaching down, leaves are reaching up, and the first tiny harvests appear. June is about watching, adjusting, and learning what each plant wants.

tasks.text: establish a watering routine — check soil daily
pinch basil tips to encourage bushiness
watch for aphids on the nasturtiums and roses
first arugula and lettuce harvests
deadhead pansies and marigolds
check if any seedlings need potting up
succession sow cilantro (it bolts fast)
feed tomatoes with liquid fertilizer

months.title: july
months.subtitle: abundance
months.narrative: This is peak season. The tomatoes are ripening, the herbs are lush, and the flowers are putting on a show. Harvest often, water deeply, and spend evenings on the balcony watching it all happen.

tasks.text: harvest tomatoes as they ripen
keep pinching basil — make pesto if there's too much
deadhead everything weekly
watch for heat stress — shade cloth if over 30°C
harvest chamomile flowers for drying
cut lavender when flowers just open — dry for sachets
water in the evening during hot spells
feed containers every 2 weeks

months.title: august
months.subtitle: deep summer
months.narrative: The garden is at its most generous. Tomatoes are going wild, herbs are at their aromatic peak, and the balcony feels like a small jungle. Enjoy it — this is what all those March mornings were for.

tasks.text: keep harvesting tomatoes — share extras with neighbours
dry herbs for winter — oregano, thyme, rosemary
harvest echinacea flowers at peak bloom
collect calendula petals for drying
sow a late round of arugula and lettuce for fall
check for powdery mildew in humid weather
make tulsi tea from fresh leaves
take a midsummer garden photo

months.title: september
months.subtitle: slowing down
months.narrative: The evenings are shorter and the mornings are cooler. The tomatoes are giving their last, the asters are just getting started, and the kale is coming into its own. Time to start thinking about wrapping up.

tasks.text: harvest remaining tomatoes — green ones ripen on windowsill
enjoy the asters and snapdragons — they love cool weather
save seeds from calendula, nasturtium, marigold
harvest valerian roots if ready (second year)
final herb harvest for drying and freezing
bring rosemary and lavender inside before first frost warning
reduce watering as temperatures drop

months.title: october
months.subtitle: putting the balcony to bed
months.narrative: The growing season is winding down. The last kale leaves are sweeter after a frost, and the balcony is getting quieter. It's time to clean up, compost, and start dreaming about next year.

tasks.text: harvest the last of everything
empty and clean all containers
compost spent soil or store for refreshing next spring
clean and store pots, trays, and tools
bring any perennials inside for winter (lavender, rosemary)
export garden data as a JSON backup
make notes about what worked and what to change next year
rest — you grew a garden on a balcony
